params.script_inline:
import sys, json, re

# THE QUESTION BACK (GH #894, R-27-3). The core called `ask_requester`: it
# cannot finish the errand without something only the one who consulted it
# knows -- a preference, a choice, a fact of the person's. The call is a HANDOFF
# in this composite's dispatcher, so the core's turn has already ended; this cell
# turns the call into what the asking surface reads: ONE sentence,
# `the core asks: <question>`, sent back under the CONSULT's id.
#
# WHY THE CONSULT'S ID AND NOT THE CALL'S. The surface correlates everything the
# core sends back by the id its own departure row was written under when the
# consult left (GH #728, OR-KX-63) -- the consult's call id, which the level's
# consult edge stamped into `context.consult_id` and which this composite never
# changes. The id of THIS call names nothing on the surface's side, and a question
# under it would arrive there anonymous, in a round of its own, and could not be
# answered under the id the surface is shown. So the context wins, and the hop's
# id (the dispatcher's `arguments.consult_id or call id`) is only the fallback
# for a core that stands outside a consult.
#
# WHY TEXT. The surface's model cannot see this core's window, so the question
# travels as the words the core wrote and never as a reference into it. A call
# whose arguments lost their JSON shape still carries a question -- its raw text
# is sent as it is -- because a silence here would leave the consult waiting for
# an answer to a question nobody heard.
#
# WHY NO BLOCK ID. The core's curator shows it every block of its window behind
# a short id, `[#<12 hex>]` (GH #892), and a model quotes what it has just read.
# An id of the core's window is a reference into a wall the surface cannot
# read, and the question goes on to a person, so it leaves here without one --
# the talky splitter's expression, by form alone, in every form a model quotes
# one, bare included, the full sixty-four-digit block id too (GH #894,
# R-27-3, OR-KY-80/81/84; one expression with the splitter's, OR-KY-83).
PREFIX = "the core asks: "
SHORT_ID = re.compile(
    r"[ \t]?(?:\[#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?: released[^\]\n]{0,64}| expired)?\]"
    r"|\[shortened[^\]\n#]{0,40}#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}[^\]\n]{0,4}\]"
    r"|\(#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}\)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#(?=[0-9]{0,15}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?!\w)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#?(?=[0-9]{0,63}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{64}(?!\w))")

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
header = ((doc.get("envelope") or {}).get("header") or {})
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
ctx = header.get("context") or {}
msgs = (doc.get("body") or {}).get("messages") or []
call = next((m for m in msgs
             if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("type") == "tool_call"), {})
raw = str(call.get("text") or "")
try:
    args = json.loads(raw or "{}")
except ValueError:
    args = None
question = ""
if isinstance(args, dict):
    question = str(args.get("question") or "").strip()
if not question:
    question = raw.strip()
question = SHORT_ID.sub("", question).strip()
if not question:
    sys.stderr.write("ask: an ask_requester call without any text -- sent as"
                     " an empty question so the consult is not left waiting\n")
consult = str(ctx.get("consult_id") or hop.get("consult_id") or "")
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "ask", "consult_id": consult,
               "tool_call_id": str(hop.get("tool_call_id") or call.get("id") or "")},
    "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                  "text": PREFIX + question}]}))

consult_id.description: the id of the consultation the question belongs to: `context.consult_id`, else the dispatcher's `hop.consult_id`. Always present, empty when neither names one -- the level's edge promotes it, and a missing hop key makes a CEL modifier fail
the consult this core is working on, stamped by the level's consult edge (GH #728)

description.purpose: The core's question back to whoever consulted it (GH #894, R-27-3). An `ask_requester` call of the core's brain becomes ONE sentence, `the core asks: <question>`, on route `ask`, under the id of the consultation the core is working on -- the id the asking surface's departure row names, so the question arrives there correlated and the surface can answer it with `reply_to_consult` under that id.
description.use_when: Inside the cogny composite, between `./dispatcher` and the rim: the dispatcher's tool emission for `ask_requester` comes here instead of leaving on the guarded default, and the `ask` this cell emits leaves the composite on the rim lane of the same name. `ask_requester` is a handoff in this composite's dispatcher, so the core's turn has ended when the question leaves.
description.not_in_scope: No answer and no waiting: the answer comes back as the core's next errand on `in_turn`, through the level's `reply_to_consult` edge, and nothing here holds state. No window reference: the question travels as the words the core wrote, because the surface cannot see the core's window -- a short block id `[#<12 hex>]` the core quoted is taken out of it.
description.emits_meaning: One message per call on route `ask`: hop.consult_id (the consultation), hop.tool_call_id (the call), and one assistant text turn `the core asks: <question>` -- the call's `question` argument, or its raw text when the arguments are not an object with one.
description.consumes_meaning: The dispatcher's tool emission for `ask_requester`: one `tool_call` turn whose text is the call's arguments, `{"question": "..."}`.
examples: tool_call {"question": "Which city are you travelling to?"} with context.consult_id 'call-c1' -> route `ask`, consult_id 'call-c1', text 'the core asks: Which city are you travelling to?'
